description: Ubuntu LTS, Node LTS, Next, React, Prisma and embedded SQLite baseline for a single-writer application delivered either as a native process or as a container image.
compatibility_rules: Exactly one application instance may write the database; this profile inherits every embedded SQLite constraint and adds a frontend framework slot on top of it.

This profile declares os, runtime, package-manager, database, framework, frontend, orm and toolchain slots. It declares no proxy, container-engine or container-compose slot, and no PostgreSQL slot; an application that needs a client-server database must move to the matching PostgreSQL profile.
A transition selects exactly one component per slot, requires an absolute http or https migration Issue plus one matching unexpired exception, and never permits a prohibited component.

A component whose deployed build differs from the catalog pin may declare as_built inside the same major, backed by one bounded exception. as_built never crosses a major, never applies to a digest-pinned image, and never suspends prohibited, EOL, expiry or checksum enforcement.

This profile allows more than one delivery contract because one repository may serve environments that differ in delivery ownership. A declaration still names exactly one contract; an application whose environments differ writes one declaration and one lock per environment rather than merging them.

A declaration that names the container delivery contract must additionally declare the catalog OCI base image component for the runtime major it ships, pinned by the catalog digest; this profile has no OCI slot because the native delivery contracts have no base image.

constraints.deployment: Delivery contracts describe delivery ownership only and grant no deployment capability; each environment is deployed by the application repository under its own Change.
constraints.data_storage: Database, WAL and shared-memory files must remain on a local filesystem on the same host; network filesystem, container ephemeral layer and multi-host access are prohibited.
constraints.concurrency: One writer; sustained lock contention, background write fan-out or more than one application instance requires PostgreSQL reassessment.
constraints.availability: No high-availability claim; host failure may require restore from backup, and a second instance is not an availability answer under this profile.
constraints.backup: Scheduled online backup using the SQLite backup API or a documented equivalent consistent snapshot, plus a retained off-host checksum, is mandatory.
constraints.restore_drill: Restore must be exercised at least semi-annually and before any schema or runtime major Change.
